text.p: Investors should hold shares of Polish meat producer Pekpol SA, which despite a promising investment programme has shown a net profit and sales dynamic below that of inflation, Bank Handlowy said in a report.

"Pekpol's financial results, to date, have been on a low level....In assuming that all of the strategic undertakings planned for future years will be realised, we are issuing a long-term hold recommendation," Handlowy said.
The report, dated February 21 and released to the media on Monday, was written when Pekpol shares cost 23.3 zlotys. The stock closed on Friday at 20.3 zlotys.
Handlowy said Pekpol's current investment programme, which should add about seven million zlotys this year from the six million in 1996, would likely help boost future earnings.
It predicted that Pekpol would lift net profit this year to 2.3 million zlotys from 1.9 million last year, and sales to 237 million zlotys from 197.3 million zlotys last year.
The stock's price-earnings ratio this year would fall to 13.4 from 16.1 at the time of the report, when the food industry's P/E was at 25.1.
Handlowy said a good sign was Pekpol's intention by the year 2000 to increase sales of its own products to 40 percent of revenues from the current 25 percent.
But it said Pekpol could suffer from the large competition on the meat products market and a high level of costs of goods sold. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
